title: Fragments of a Rainy Day
summary: A diary piece about scattered impressions, reflective surfaces, and the loose narrative of bad weather.
main_text:
Rain has a way of editing memory before the day is even over. That was the feeling I had moving through these pieces: not a complete story, but fragments connected by shine, blur, and hesitation. Wet streets, silver windows, and coats darkened at the shoulder kept returning in different forms.

What interested me most was how little the works needed to declare. A reflective patch of pavement could stand in for a whole afternoon. A bent umbrella at the edge of a sketch suggested mood more effectively than any dramatic figure. The fragments were enough because rain already teaches the eye to assemble partial information.

By the time I finished the room, I felt as though I had remembered someone else's day in pieces. That incomplete quality was exactly what made the work persuasive. It trusted the viewer to supply the weather between the lines.
